events.title: Madras Is Founded
events.description: The British East India Company acquired a narrow strip of coastal land from local Nayak rulers and founded a settlement there. It later became the city of Madras, now Chennai.
events.significance: The settlement became a major hub of British power in India and grew into one of the country's largest cities.

events.title: Charles I Raises His Standard at Nottingham
events.description: King Charles I raised his royal standard in Nottingham, a traditional signal that he was calling his supporters to arms against Parliament.
events.significance: It marked the start of the English Civil War, which led to the king's execution and a brief end to the monarchy.

events.title: The Haitian Revolution Begins
events.description: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose up in a revolt that grew into a full-scale revolution.
events.significance: It led to the first successful large-scale slave revolt in modern history and the founding of Haiti as an independent nation.

events.title: The First Geneva Convention Is Signed
events.description: Twelve nations signed an agreement setting out rules to protect the wounded and those caring for them in wartime.
events.significance: It laid the groundwork for modern international humanitarian law and the work of the Red Cross.

events.title: Roosevelt Rides in an Automobile and Cadillac Is Founded
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt became the first U.S. president to appear in public in a car. The Cadillac Motor Company was also founded on the same day.
events.significance: The day marked the arrival of the automobile in American public life and the birth of a lasting luxury car brand.
